title: Prevent lid closure from interrupting shutdown
head: bedc2a39792d
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: The caller still schedules a worker from OMARCHY_PATH rather than the script it actually ran
leads.consequence: The $0 change fixes a stale OMARCHY_PATH only inside the already launched --inhibit service. If the invoking shell's OMARCHY_PATH points to a different checkout from the script actually invoked (for example explicitly invoking the packaged /usr/bin/omarchy-system-shutdown in a dev-linked session), line 31 runs that other checkout's worker. If it holds the base version, its --inhibit argument is ignored, it schedules the original unprotected 2-second poweroff timer, and closing the lid can still suspend instead. If that checkout was removed, systemd-run refuses the missing executable before starting a service; no preparation, inhibitor, notification or poweroff follows. The nine-test fixture overwrites OMARCHY_PATH with ROOT before the first call and only injects a stale value after capturing the worker, so it misses both cases. The base shutdown scheduled systemctl without consulting OMARCHY_PATH. Consider using $0 for the outer service command too; systemd-run resolves bare PATH and relative paths into absolute paths for local calls.
leads.triage: Opus found same (case D), pre-existing since first commit, repo convention, fails only when caller env is broken; internal-mode direct invocation not a production route; not published

leads.summary: Integrate #10353's session freeze with both shutdown stages, including asynchronous failure cleanup
leads.consequence: Open PR #10353 calls omarchy-session prepare-exit before closing windows and removes its exiting marker only on immediate scheduling failure. These shutdown scripts have a genuine merge conflict. Retaining #13076's script without moving prepare-exit loses #10353's final snapshot. Adding prepare-exit only to the caller but keeping the new asynchronous service leaves the marker when systemd-inhibit or systemctl fails after the caller has returned, suppressing subsequent automatic snapshots until next startup. Integrate capture before preparation and cancel-exit in the worker's error path. #10353's own system-power test also conflicts with the rewritten fixture.

leads.summary: #9520's close-all wait and 15-second shutdown timer need redesign with the new two-second worker
leads.consequence: Open PR #9520 extends the window-close helper with a bounded --wait (default 10 seconds), then arms shutdown 15 seconds out so apps can flush. Its shutdown-script hunk conflicts with #13076. Resolving by keeping #13076's immediate two-second poweroff discards #9520's waiting guarantee, whether the helper is called without --wait or moved to background with --wait. #9520's new system-shutdown-test.sh expects a shutdown --on-active timer and fails against this head even when its helper is added. Resolve by coordinating both timings and changing the invariant test, not only by resolving text conflicts.

leads.summary: The current overlap list includes #11151's shutdown user-bus fallback, whose service semantics cannot be mechanically retained
leads.consequence: Open PR #11151 adds a fallback from user to system manager when a user bus is absent, in both shutdown and reboot. #13076 still uses only systemd-run --user, and the shutdown code and power fixture genuinely conflict. Keeping this PR's script loses the new shutdown fallback. Blindly copying #11151's --system fallback for this PR's worker changes the worker's execution to the system manager context, where its user notification and desktop commands no longer have the same user session. Integration requires specifying the intended user/session environment or keeping fallback only for the independent reboot path; neither PR is stacked on the other.
leads.triage: also in Opus final; coordinator verified #11151 diff via gh; published as optional note

leads.summary: Outside stop of the bounded service does not enter shutdown's failure-notification handler
leads.consequence: The handler only runs after systemd-inhibit returns. A stop by RuntimeMaxSec=30s or a separate systemctl stop begins killing the unit containing the inhibitor parent and shell rather than letting the inhibitor return normally. The user does not receive the critical failure toast even though no poweroff was requested; next invocation can be retried. This is an existing R2 optional note, not introduced by the $0 edit. No assertion in the nine focused tests simulates an external service stop.

leads.summary: Reconcile the logout and legacy OSD fixture PRs against the new power-test format
leads.consequence: #12254 adds logout assertions to system-power-test.sh using the old shared assert_power_calls helper, which this PR removes. Their test changes conflict, so taking only one side loses coverage or leaves the other side's tests failing. #12575 and #7216 independently add OSD stubs to the old fixture and conflict at the same lines; the head already has an OSD stub, so those test-only changes need deduplication. No additional production behavior is claimed for these fixture-only overlaps.
leads.triage: routine textual conflicts; Opus concurs; not published

limits: Source review at pinned systemd v261.3 establishes the actual argument, lifetime and path behavior; real desktop/system services were not touched. No valid conflict-free combined tree exists for #9520/#10353/#11151/#12254 without manual resolution, so their hypothetical integration tests were not run; claims above are conditional on the stated resolutions.

flags.claim: The service's `OMARCHY_PATH` no longer plays any part.
flags.why: It no longer selects the worker script, but the worker still runs helpers in the service environment: omarchy-osd calls `omarchy-shell -q osd show` (bin/omarchy-osd:40), and omarchy-shell requires and uses `$OMARCHY_PATH` to find the running shell (bin/omarchy-shell:40-41, 59). So the service's OMARCHY_PATH still decides where the OSD IPC goes. That is harmless (the user manager's value matches the shell started with the session) and unchanged from the base, but the absolute wording is too strong.

flags.claim: Symlinked install paths such as `/usr/share/omarchy/bin` stay as spelled and still run.
flags.why: 'Stay as spelled' is from source (open_and_check_executable does not chase symlinks when root is NULL, sd-v261.3/src/basic/path-util.c:666-683, 696-705). 'Still run' was tested only with a symlinked checkout directory (probe case F, run 20260928T061615Z-39a3b6f2), not with `/usr/share/omarchy/bin`'s per-file symlinks. That those are symlinks comes from docs/file-layout.md, not from the PKGBUILD. The conclusion is very likely right (execve through a file symlink traverses it the same way), but the example goes beyond what was run.

flags.claim: The worker is now `"$0" --inhibited`, the same absolute path the caller passed to `systemd-run`.
flags.why: Strictly, `$0` is the path the caller passed, made absolute against the caller's cwd and simplified by systemd-run (path_make_absolute_cwd + path_simplify, sd-v261.3/src/basic/path-util.c:696-705). With the absolute OMARCHY_PATH that env-bootstrap and omarchy-dev-link always write, the two are identical, and line 15 states the absolutising step. Fine to leave.

flags.claim: It keeps the base timer and adds a `systemd-run --system` fallback when the user bus is unavailable.
flags.why: #11151's code falls back whenever the `systemd-run --user` call fails, for any reason; 'when no user bus is available' is its comment's stated intent. It also exports XDG_RUNTIME_DIR and DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS when missing (git diff of pr/11151 for bin/omarchy-system-shutdown). Describing it by intent is reasonable.

flags.claim: The related-PR list gains one entry, below
flags.why: Correct as an editorial choice matching my recommendation. Not exhaustive: #7216, #12575 (power-test OSD stubs), #7434 and #11010 (OSD string translations in shutdown/reboot) also edit these files and conflict textually at both eaaca77 and bedc2a3 (gh/open-pr-files.json, git merge-tree). The wording does not claim completeness, so no change is needed.

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

Follow-up to the [earlier follow-up review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/13076#issuecomment-5854851897) and the [author's reply](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/13076#issuecomment-5856715423), checked at `bedc2a3`.

**Verified:** the worker-path point is resolved. No regressions were found in the new commit.

| Earlier point | Status at `bedc2a3` |
|---|---|
| Worker path came from the user manager's `OMARCHY_PATH` | **Resolved.** The worker is now `"$0" --inhibited`, the same absolute path the caller passed to `systemd-run` |
| Optional notes (external stop sends no notification, reboot keeps the timer design, related open PRs) | Unchanged by this commit. The related-PR list gains one entry, below |

**Verified** for the new commit:
- `systemd-run` makes the executable path absolute against the caller's working directory without resolving symlinks, and the service manager execs that path directly (systemd v261.3 and v262 source). In `--inhibit` mode, `$0` is therefore the path the caller expanded. The service's `OMARCHY_PATH` no longer selects the worker script.
- In a sandbox emulation with the service `OMARCHY_PATH` pointing at a missing directory, the head script ran its own worker and reached `systemctl poweroff`. The `eaaca77` line instead failed with "No such file or directory" and sent "Shutdown failed".
- Launching through `PATH`, `omarchy shutdown`, `omarchy system shutdown` or a relative path all passed the same absolute path to `systemd-run`. A symlinked checkout path stays as spelled and still runs.

**Author claims:** all confirmed.
- The new stale-`OMARCHY_PATH` test fails in 5 of 5 runs when only the `eaaca77` shutdown script is restored, and passes on the head.
- The test file emits exactly 9 `ok` lines. It passed in 10 of 10 sequential and 24 of 24 concurrent sandbox runs.

**Optional notes:**
- Open PR #11151 ("Fall back when reboot has no session D-Bus") also edits `bin/omarchy-system-shutdown` and the power test. It keeps the base timer and adds a `systemd-run --system` fallback when the `--user` call fails, for example without a user bus. This PR schedules only through `systemd-run --user`, so combining the two needs a decision on whether that fallback carries over to the new service.
- The PR description still says "Eight focused tests pass". There are now nine.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Source review of the `eaaca77..bedc2a3` change, the shutdown script's callers and the `omarchy` dispatcher, systemd v261.3 and v262 `systemd-run`, service-manager exec and `systemd-inhibit` code, and related open PRs at their current heads. The PR's `test/shell.d/system-power-test.sh` ran in an isolated sandbox with stubbed power commands, alongside a copy with only the earlier shutdown script restored and an emulation of the service's final exec. No real `systemd-run`, user manager, `systemd-inhibit`, logind, notification daemon or hardware was exercised. The external-stop note was not re-run, because nothing on that path changed.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical follow-up review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.

**Opt out:** To stop receiving these reviews, reply to this comment saying so.
